activities.caption: true or false — what counts as excretion
activities.name: exEgestionJudge

statements.s: Excretion is the removal from the body of the waste products of metabolism.
statements.why: Metabolic waste — not undigested food, which leaves by a different door.

statements.s: Passing undigested food out of the gut is excretion.
statements.why: It never entered a cell or took part in metabolism — that is egestion.

statements.s: The lungs excrete carbon dioxide and the kidneys excrete urea, excess water and excess ions.
statements.why: Two organs do almost all of the body's excreting.

statements.s: Faeces are a major route for clearing urea from the blood.
statements.why: Urea rides the blood to the kidneys; urea is toxic and must not accumulate.

activities.name: exPlumbingMatch

pairs.right: the kidney's outer and inner regions
drain urine down to the bladder

config.why: Fist-sized filters at 0.4% of body mass consume ~7% of resting ATP — one of the most energetically demanding operations in the body.

activities.anchor: why the liver bothers with the two-step ammonia-to-urea detour
activities.caption: toxicity against water cost — drag between the two molecules
activities.name: exAmmoniaCompare

config.prompt: The nitrogen-excretion trade-off — drag the divider:

before.label: ammonia
before.text: Small and extremely soluble — and extremely toxic: it would poison nerve cells at low concentrations and demands large volumes of water to flush.

after.label: urea
after.text: Far less toxic — it rides the blood at useful concentrations, and the kidneys choose how much water to spend excreting it.

config.why: The same logic shaped uric acid in birds and insects — safer still, but energetically dearer to make. Excretion and water balance can never be discussed separately.

activities.anchor: Each kidney packs about a million
activities.caption: rebuild the nephron's two moves
activities.name: exNephronOrder

config.prompt: Filter, then re-choose — put the nephron's work in order:
items: Blood pressure in the glomerulus forces water, glucose, urea and ions into Bowman's capsule
Blood cells, platelets and proteins stay behind — anything above ~68,000 mass cannot pass
The proximal tubule hauls back all the glucose, some ions and most water by active transport
The loop of Henle and collecting duct finish the water balance
What remains — urea, excess water, excess ions — is urine
config.why: The nephron never decides at the filter, only at the reabsorber: about half the filtered urea is passively reabsorbed anyway, but the rest is left in the tubule deliberately.

activities.anchor: detected by osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the water thermostat
activities.name: exADHCloze

config.text: ADH is released by the %%0%% when blood becomes too concentrated, detected by %%1%% in the hypothalamus, and makes the %%2%% %%3%% more permeable to water. Alcohol %%4%% ADH release — which is why beer dehydrates while it appears to hydrate.
config.hint: The loop closes: any deviation in blood concentration automatically calls up its own correction.

activities.anchor: no glucose, no protein, no blood cells
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the urine report
activities.name: exUrineSpot

config.prompt: This urine-analysis answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Normal urine is about 95% water and 2% urea, with no glucose, no protein and no blood cells.
Glucose in urine means plasma exceeded the renal threshold of about 180 mg/dL.
Protein in urine means the glomerular filter itself is leaking.
Blood or pus cells point to infection, stones or injury elsewhere in the tract.
Dark, scanty urine means the ADH loop has switched off entirely — you are overhydrated.
config.correction: Dark, scanty urine means the ADH loop is SQUEEZING HARD — you are dehydrated and the kidney is protecting you.
config.why: The dipstick is selective reabsorption read backwards: whatever shows up in the urine is whatever the nephron failed to keep.

activities.anchor: The whole apparatus is dialysis by another name
activities.caption: run the failure clinic — choose the management
activities.name: exFailureBranch

config.root: The nephrons are failing — urea and ions climb, water balance collapses. Untreated, days to weeks. Choose the management.

start.text: Which option do you set up?

choices.label: Haemodialysis machine
choices.feedback: Blood over a selectively permeable membrane against fresh dialysis fluid.

choices.label: Peritoneal dialysis
choices.feedback: The patient's own abdominal lining as the membrane.

choices.label: Transplant a donor kidney
choices.feedback: The machine becomes unnecessary — at a price.

machine.text: The dialysate is the therapeutic art: glucose at blood levels prevents sugar loss, ion levels set each ion's diffusion direction, and it is refreshed fast enough to keep urea's gradient steep. Three to four sessions a week, four hours each.

peri.text: Portable and able to run overnight — less efficient than a machine, but closer to the continuous, gentle correction a real kidney performs.

transplant.text: One kidney at 60–80% of a pair's filtration is enough — the safety margin was built for this — but the recipient takes immunosuppressants for life: the new kidney is genetically somebody else's.

config.why: Dialysis and transplant both reimpose the filter-everything, keep-what-matters design — the machine does for a few hours what a million nephrons do continuously.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — the loop's ceiling
activities.name: exRodentEstimate

config.prompt: The loop of Henle's countercurrent gradient reaches about 1,200 mOsm in human medullas — roughly 4 times blood. Desert rodents concentrate urine to over how many times blood concentration?
config.why: Over 20 times, against the human 4 — the loop's length sets the ceiling, which is why anatomy is destiny in osmoregulation.
config.context: ADH decides how many aquaporin water channels stand open; full open and the fluid equilibrates with the deep medulla.
